thread_analysis.thread_summary: Allied Telesis K.K. (contact Masayuki Ogawa, Software Development Dept.) consults Allion (Masaya Iida, with technical answers drafted by Itsuo Sakai) about Bluetooth SIG certification for a GEN2 device, spanning an initial cost/timeline quote, a dispute over a conflicting 'not certifiable' assessment from another certification body, and a QDID combination correction to avoid an AoA/AoD capability mismatch via a matching Subset DN.
all_questions_found: (Administrative) What's the cost and timeline estimate for full RF-PHY testing and registration?
Is another certification body's 'not certifiable' assessment of a previously-suggested QDID combination correct? (see thread_0015_case_01)
Can a specific Link Layer/Host QDID be registered with the customer's RF PHY QDID, and if not, what's the alternative? (see thread_0015_case_02)
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: This thread illustrates that the mere presence of a cross-layer Consistency Check inconsistency doesn't automatically disqualify registration (registrability depends on specific conditions tied to how the reference QDID was originally registered), and that capability mismatches (like AoA/AoD support) between Link Layer/Host and RF PHY components can often be resolved by referencing a narrower-capability Subset DN under the same base registration rather than abandoning the registration attempt.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified — Allion correctly distinguished the technical fact (an inconsistency exists) from the broader conclusion (registration is blocked), pushing back constructively on another certification body's incomplete assessment.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a customer raises a conflicting registrability assessment from another certification body, or proposes a QDID combination with a capability mismatch, independently verify the specific registration mechanics (inherited-inconsistency conditions, available Subset DNs) rather than accepting a blanket conclusion or giving up on the registration attempt.
